mainEntity.name: Why is the slope of a vertical line undefined?

acceptedAnswer.text: A vertical line has Δx = 0, so the slope formula divides by zero. Its angle is 90° and its equation is x = a, rather than y = mx + b.

mainEntity.name: How is slope related to the derivative?

acceptedAnswer.text: The derivative dy/dx is the slope of the tangent line to a curve at a point. For a straight line the slope is constant, so the derivative equals m everywhere.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between percent slope, degrees and roof pitch?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are the same steepness in different units. Percent slope is 100 × rise ÷ run; degrees are arctan(rise ÷ run); pitch is rise per 12 units of run. A 12% slope is 6.84°, or a pitch of 1.44 in 12. They are not proportional: 100% slope is 45°, not 100°.

mainEntity.name: How do I find a perpendicular or parallel slope?

acceptedAnswer.text: A parallel line has the same slope m. A perpendicular line has slope −1 ÷ m (the negative reciprocal). If m = 0 the perpendicular line is vertical, and vice versa.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert Ax + By = C to y = mx + b?

acceptedAnswer.text: Solve for y: y = (−A ÷ B)x + C ÷ B, provided B ≠ 0. If B = 0 the line is vertical at x = C ÷ A.

mainEntity.name: Can slope be a fraction or a decimal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Slope is any real number. It is often best left as an exact fraction such as 2/3, because the decimal 0.6667 is only an approximation.
